sentences.text: Though the Respondent No.1 has taken contentions that on the alleged date of accident, there was triple riding in the Petitioner's motorcycle, it has not produced any documents to prove the said fact.
The Charge-sheet does not shows on the alleged date of accident, there was triple riding in the motorcycle.

Under such circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioners have proved the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry and the Petitioner Harshavardhan Reddy had sustained grievous injuries and the said Mohan Reddy was succumbed to the injuries sustained in the said accident.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in both cases in the "Affirmative".
23. Issue No.2 in MVC No.4412/2017:- As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the SCCH 15 17 MVC No.4412 & 4413/2017 rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
24. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 33 years.
Ex.P-17 is the Aadhaar card of the Petitioner which shows the birth year of the Petitioner was 1983.
The alleged accident taken place on 23.02.2017.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner at the time of accident is to be 34 years.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident to be taken at 34 years for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
25. Further, the Petitioner has averred that he was working as an Associate Team Member at SLK Global Solutions Pvt. Ltd., and was drawing a salary of Rs.15,000/- p.m.
The Petitioner has produced his Statement of Account at Ex.P16 and Offer Letter at Ex.P23.
Upon going through the said documents Ex.P23 shows that the Petitioner was offered for the job of Associate Team Member in SLK Global Solutions Pvt. Ltd., for monthly Gross salary at Rs.10,022/-.
The said document also SCCH 15 18 MVC No.4412 & 4413/2017 shows that basic salary is Rs.8,300/-.
The statutory bonus shows Rs.1,660/- and other allowances.
The Petitioner has not examined the officials of the SLK Global Solutions Pvt. Ltd.

Hence, by relying on the Ex.P23 i.e., basic salary of the Petitioner i.e.,
Rs.8,300/- to be taken for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
26. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
31.
The Petitioner deposed in his evidence that he has taken treatment as an inpatient at Bengaluru Baptist hospital.
Ex-P20 is the Discharge Summary which shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient from 24.02.2017 to 11.03.2017.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 18 days.
32. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as three months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled SCCH 15 21 MVC No.4412 & 4413/2017 for compensation of Rs.24,900/- under this head (@ Rs.8,300/- per month ).
IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
33.

Admittedly, the Petitioner had sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.9,000/- (@ Rs.100/- per day) towards attendants charges, Rs.9,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.9,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.27,000/- under this head.
